notes: Arabic omits 'to be' in simple present-tense sentences. كَانَ is used to put a sentence into the past tense (and its present form يَكُونُ yakūnu is used for the future or after modal words).
The noun or adjective that follows كَانَ as its predicate takes the accusative case (-an): كَانَ الطَّقْسُ جَمِيلًا (The weather was nice).
